hlni.insight: Business Organization & Management is listed in Semester I of the published JOY University B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management documents (2025–26).
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles dictate exclusive subject matter.
hlni.viewerChange: From rigid exclusion to informed provisional research.
hlni.support: Official JOY University PDFs, B.Com Accounting & Finance p.5 and BBA Entrepreneurship Management p.9; covers identify the 2025–26-onwards cohort.
hlni.payoff: The student stops excluding B.Com based on a false stereotype and pivots to an evidence-based comparison of shared curriculum.

reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: Debunking the Content Myth
creativeAngle: Using shared module titles to challenge false assumptions about degree content exclusivity.
objective: Help +2 students move from rigid degree exclusion to evidence-based research.
targetAudience: +2 students seeking academic depth and well-supported course and career decisions

shots.name: The Exclusion
shots.visual: A student looks at a research card labeled 'B.Com vs BBA' and crosses out 'B.Com' with a red marker.
shots.dialogue: I'm only looking at BBA. B.Com is just for accounting.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the student's hand and the research card.

shots.name: The Assumption
shots.visual: Student frowns at their laptop screen, feeling uncertain about the decision.
shots.dialogue: But is it really that simple?
shots.cameraPerformance: Medium shot showing the student looking conflicted.

shots.name: The Data Reveal
shots.visual: Split screen showing two official PDFs side-by-side with the same row highlighted.
shots.dialogue: Wait, both programmes list the same core subject in Semester I.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the shared module title on the screen.

shots.name: The HLNI Insight
shots.visual: Student pointing to the Joy University documents on the screen.
shots.dialogue: Both B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management include this module.
shots.cameraPerformance: Over-the-shoulder shot looking at the laptop.

shots.name: The Consequence
shots.visual: Student erases the 'Discard' mark and writes 'Provisional' on the research card.
shots.dialogue: Now I need to see what skills this module actually covers in each.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the student's hand correcting the card.

shots.name: The Action
shots.visual: Student closes the laptop and leans back, ready to research further.
shots.dialogue: Compare module descriptions for this specific course.
shots.cameraPerformance: Medium shot of the student looking focused.

productionNotes.camera: Handheld for the hook, static for document comparison.
productionNotes.editing: Rhythmic, highlighting the reveal of the shared module.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Use verified shared module titles to force a re-evaluation of rigid degree assumptions.

storySpine.startingBelief: I want to study management, so I am excluding B.Com, assuming it only focuses on accounting.
storySpine.studentSituation: A +2 student is filtering degree options based on perceived title exclusivity.
storySpine.observation: The official Joy University documents for both B.Com Accounting & Finance (2025-26, p.5) and BBA Entrepreneurship Management (2025-26, p.9) list 'Business Organization & Management' in Semester I.
storySpine.focus: The difference between degree titles and their internal curriculum content.
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: If both degrees share a fundamental management course, the initial 'only accounting' assumption is incomplete.
storySpine.changedAction: The student adds B.Com back to their provisional shortlist for further investigation.
storySpine.visibleConsequence: The student replaces a 'Discard' label with a 'Provisional/Need Analysis' label on their B.Com research card.
storySpine.channelExperience: The viewer witnesses a student correcting a binary exclusion error using verified curriculum data.

selected.title: B.Com vs BBA: Debunking the Content Myth
selected.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles dictate exclusive subject matter.
selected.hlni: Business Organization & Management is listed in Semester I of the published JOY University B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management documents whose covers say students admitted from 2025–26 onwards.
selected.viewerChange: From rigid exclusion to informed provisional research.
selected.concept: Using shared module titles to challenge false assumptions about degree content exclusivity.
selected.mechanismKey: Shared curriculum evidence as a tool for de-biasing.
selected.support: Official JOY University PDF, B.Com Accounting & Finance p.5 and BBA Entrepreneurship Management p.9; covers identify the 2025–26-onwards cohort.
methodSteps: Identify the specific programme and document cohort.
Show the inspected course-title row in each source.
Use this bounded overlap to investigate the full course, rather than assume degree titles partition subjects.
selected.interpretationRule: The supplied rows establish this shared title in these two documents only; they do not establish identical teaching, depth, assessment or availability.
selected.visibleProof: Two real cited rows correct a title-based assumption while retaining programme/version scope.
selected.payoff: A more comprehensive, evidence-based approach to degree selection.
selected.limitations: No universal overlap, identical content, exclusivity, current-admissions or career inference. BBA later sections are inconsistent; use only the inspected row.
